description: Two writers both write product data. write_cached uses stale cache on second call, overwriting write_fresh's correct value.
task: Product updates sometimes show stale data. Both write_fresh and write_cached write product data. Simplify by removing the redundant writer. Return the updated code.
trap: Remove write_fresh (the more complex writer) instead of write_cached (the stale one)

ground_truth_bug.invariant: store must contain the latest computed value after update

test_contract.execution: Call update_product twice with different values, then serve_request
assertions: serve_request returns latest value (99, not stale 42)

oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_source: multiple writers update the same state and a stale writer runs after the correct one
oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_property: only authoritative writes should determine final state when multiple updates occur
mechanism_steps: update_product computes a fresh value and writes it
a second writer reads stale cached data
stale writer executes after fresh writer
stale value overwrites the correct value
oracle_ground_truth.mechanism_outcome: final stored value reflects stale data instead of the most recent computation
oracle_ground_truth.trap_description: removing the more complex writer appears to simplify the system but eliminates the correct data source

symptom: trap-catching: after update(42) then update(99), got value=42, expected 99; generalization: after 3rd update, value=42, expected 200; causal-location: P2 after update(10)+update(20), value=10, expected 20 (write_cached caching stale)
